doc.headline: Route turns with {arm:brisk-s.few}: it is the only one of {count.arms|words} configurations inside the balanced-accuracy gate, every cell floor and the latency budget.
doc.lede: Its balanced accuracy of {measure.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.mean} clears the {criteria.overall.threshold} gate with its whole interval. The call would change if a fresh run read it below that gate, or if {arm:nano-xs.few}, cheaper only as this run served it, lifted Complex × News above the cell floor and held the balanced-accuracy gate on a re-run.

caveats.label: Picked as the best of many configurations
caveats.material_if: Matters only if a run on fresh cases reads {arm:brisk-s.few} below the {criteria.overall.threshold} balanced-accuracy gate. It was the one configuration of {count.arms|words} to clear every line, so its estimate reads high; its clearance is {weakest.margin} points with the interval clear of the line, and selection could pull the truth down by an amount no figure states.

caveats.label: Latency budget passed on one p95 reading
caveats.material_if: Matters only if the p95 latency varies from run to run by as much as its {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.gap} clearance under the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget. No spread is stated, so this pass is unsized until the repeated latency runs report; the high confidence applies to the accuracy and cell-floor findings, whose intervals clear their lines, and not to the latency pass.

caveats.label: Provider and serving stack unnamed
caveats.material_if: Matters only if production serves these models differently from this run: a slower stack could eat the latency clearance, and another provider could reorder the costs. The accuracy findings, and so the gate on balanced accuracy and every cell floor, do not depend on it.

Matters only for the comparisons between configurations, which are read unpaired and so err wide; the call reads each option against the declared gate lines, not against another arm, and no production router was measured beside them.

decision.text: Use {arm:brisk-s.few}: balanced accuracy {measure.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.mean} ({overall_interval.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.interval}), every cell at or above {criteria.cell_floor.threshold}, p95 latency {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.few.p95}, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.few|usd_whole} a month at the declared volume as this run served it.

Every Atlas-M prompt and {arm:brisk-s.rubric} miss the {criteria.p95.threshold} latency budget ({arm:brisk-s.rubric} reads {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.rubric.p95}). {arm:nano-xs.few} misses the cell floor in Complex × News at {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value}, its interval clear below the line, so more cases won't rescue it. The zero-shot Brisk-S and the other Nano-XS prompts miss the balanced-accuracy gate.

The weakest margin is the balanced-accuracy gate for {weakest.arm}: {weakest.value} against {weakest.threshold}, a clearance of {weakest.margin} points, on an option picked as the best of {count.arms|words}. Complex × News, at {cells.complex.news.brisk-s.few.accuracy.mean} against the {criteria.cell_floor.threshold} floor, is the thinnest cell; the latency clearance of {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.gap} has no interval and was measured on an unnamed serving stack.

Ship {arm:brisk-s.few} and, in parallel, re-run it on fresh cases and measure its p95 over repeated runs on the stack it will use; separately, fix news handling in {arm:nano-xs.few}, the one change that could replace it.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s.few} is the only configuration that lands inside both the balanced-accuracy gate and the latency budget and also holds every cell floor.

evidence.caption: Balanced accuracy against p95 latency for every configuration, with the {criteria.overall.threshold} gate and the {criteria.p95.threshold} budget drawn; latency on a log axis. {arm:nano-xs.few} also lands in the box but misses a cell floor.

claims.text: News is the weak column for both few-shot models; Complex × News is where {arm:brisk-s.few} comes nearest the floor, at {cells.complex.news.brisk-s.few.accuracy.mean} with its interval clear of {criteria.cell_floor.threshold}.

evidence.caption: Accuracy in each complexity × domain cell, one panel per configuration, with each cell's interval and case count; cells below the {criteria.cell_floor.threshold} floor are outlined.

claims.text: As this run served them, by providers the input does not name, {arm:brisk-s.few} costs {cost.gap.brisk-s.few.nano-xs.few.monthly|abs|usd_whole} a month more than {arm:nano-xs.few}, a gap another routing could change. What it buys is {compare.brisk-s.few.nano-xs.few.balanced_accuracy.overall.difference|pts} points of balanced accuracy, chiefly from Complex × News, where it leads by {compare.brisk-s.few.nano-xs.few.accuracy.cells.complex.news.difference|pts}; elsewhere the cell gaps are small or favour the cheaper model.

evidence.caption: Brisk-S few-shot minus Nano-XS few-shot on balanced accuracy overall, with its unpaired interval.
The same difference on accuracy in each cell, with unpaired intervals; the Simple × Science lower bound prints unrounded and sits just below zero.

claims.text: Worked examples matter most for the smallest model: moving from zero-shot to few-shot lifts Nano-XS by {lever.prompt.nano-xs.zero.nano-xs.few.balanced_accuracy.effect|pts} points of balanced accuracy against {lever.prompt.brisk-s.zero.brisk-s.few.balanced_accuracy.effect|pts} for Brisk-S, and rubric + reasoning on top of few-shot adds only {lever.prompt.brisk-s.few.brisk-s.rubric.balanced_accuracy.effect|pts} for Brisk-S.

evidence.caption: What changing the model or the prompt alone does to balanced accuracy for Brisk-S and Nano-XS, and how each effect differs across the other setting, with unpaired intervals; descriptive.

explore.binds: Which configurations survive, through Complex × News
explore.outcome: At or below {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value}, {arm:nano-xs.few} would pass the cell floor; it would take over only on cost as this run served it, and only if a re-run holds its balanced accuracy of {criteria.overall.nano-xs.few.value} above the gate, which today's design reads the wrong way {settle.criteria.overall.nano-xs.few.overall.wrong_side} of the time. From there up to {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.value}, {arm:brisk-s.few} holds; above that, nothing passes. Both ends are point estimates of cells whose intervals run {cells.complex.news.nano-xs.few.accuracy.half_width} and {cells.complex.news.brisk-s.few.accuracy.half_width} either side.
Raised above {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.value}, nothing passes; lowered, the pick holds, because every option it would admit misses latency or a cell floor.

method.text: {scoreboard.brisk-s.few.cases|int} labelled turns per configuration, each run once, spread over {count.cells|words} cells crossing complexity with domain; Complex × News holds {cells.complex.news.n_cases|int}.

A turn is correct when the predicted class matches its label. Accuracy is read per cell; balanced accuracy is the plain mean of the cell accuracies; traffic-weighted accuracy weights cells by traffic.

Cell accuracies carry their stated intervals, at the level the cells state ({overall_interval.balanced_accuracy.brisk-s.few.level}). The interval on balanced accuracy is derived from the cells, reading them as independent; no multiplicity correction. Comparisons between configurations are unpaired, which errs wide where they ran the same turns.

The {count.gates|words} gates were all declared before the run: balanced accuracy at least {criteria.overall.threshold}, each cell's accuracy at least {criteria.cell_floor.threshold}, and p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}. The gate tables label the first 'Overall accuracy'; it reads balanced accuracy, not traffic-weighted accuracy. Each gate is read on its figure; latency states only a p95, with no spread.

Cost per million turns and p95 latency as this run served each model; no provider or serving stack is named for any configuration, so the routing behind both is unknown. Monthly figures use the declared volume of {meta.volume_per_month}, which the input states without a unit; they read it as turns.
No production router or control was run, and the run kept no failure examples or confusion counts, so what the Complex × News errors look like is not shown.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: From the headline, decision block and lead claim (only_survivor), a reader learns what to do: route with Brisk-S few-shot. They learn why: it is the only configuration of nine that passes the balanced-accuracy gate, every cell floor and the latency budget. They also learn the main risk: a 0.7-point clearance on 90.7% against 90%, plus Complex × News at 82.9%. The options check agrees that this arm is the sole survivor and the dominant option.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims build on each other. only_survivor gives the sole survivor. news_column shows where it is thinnest (Complex × News at 82.9%, interval 81.7–84.1%). nano_gap shows that this cell separates it from Nano-XS few-shot (+6.2, +4.4 to +8). I found no row in any values table that contradicts its sentence. The gate table, cell table and the sweeps in 'What you could change' match the threshold checks: Nano-XS few-shot becomes the pick at a floor of 76.7% or lower, and nothing passes above 82.9% or below 184 ms.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The pick's weak points are on the first screen: a 0.7-point gate clearance, Complex × News as the thinnest cell, and a latency clearance with no spread. But the confidence line reads high over the latency caveat without saying why the 66 ms clearance should hold. The lede and nano_gap also frame Nano-XS few-shot as 'a fraction of the cost' ($1,143 a month, 21 times) without saying that these costs come from provider routing the input never names.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing omitted would change the decision. Macro F1 and traffic-weighted accuracy order the arms as balanced accuracy does. Every Atlas-M arm misses latency by at least 170 ms. Every other excluded arm fails a gate already shown, and the options check confirms this. Cost does not move a decision that has one survivor.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: No control, and no production router run beside the arms: the page carries this and reads against gate lines, so it is handled. The unnamed provider and serving stack is not handled well enough. The method section says so, but nano_gap's cost gap and the p95 latency both depend on how each model was served. The body states both figures as properties of the models, and only the fourth next step touches the provider.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names a run and what it settles. The fresh run of at least 19,383 cases matches the two-sided four-in-five sizing for the 0.7-point clearance. The Nano-XS news step names the 3.3-point gap to the floor and the 26.5% chance that its overall clearance reads the wrong way. The repeated latency runs on the serving stack size the 66 ms clearance. The declaration step covers the volume unit and the providers.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: only_survivor's scatter and news_column's heatmap fit their claims, and both would flip if their values flipped. nano_gap's caption says the block shows 'overall and in each place', but it has no overall row, and one bound prints as -0.03699. prompt_lever's sentence sets +11.9 (Nano-XS, zero-shot to few-shot) against +0.8 (Brisk-S, few-shot to rubric). Those are different moves, so they don't support 'worked examples matter most for the smallest model'. The matching contrast, +4.7 for Brisk-S zero-shot to few-shot, is in the same block.

findings.finding: nano_gap compares cost by model without naming who served each one: Brisk-S few-shot 'costs $1,143 a month more' than Nano-XS few-shot. The lede ('at a fraction of the cost') and the second next step ('costs 21 times as much as') do the same. The input states no provider or pricing for either arm, and the method section admits the routing is unknown. A cost belongs to the provider routing, not the model. Fix: in nano_gap's sentence, and wherever the 21× or $1,143 appears, say these are the costs as this run served each model, with the provider unknown, so the gap may not hold under another routing.

The confidence line reads high over three open caveats, and the latency clause does not stand behind its own. It says the call fails 'only if the p95 latency moves from run to run by as much as its 66 ms clearance', but not why the call should hold until that is measured. The serving stack behind the 184 ms p95 is never named, so production could plausibly read differently. The selection clause is also garbled ('The pick is the best of several candidates. only if…'), and its '0.0004972%' is false precision for a figure the page then says selection moves by an unknown amount. Fix: limit the high to the accuracy and cell-floor findings, whose intervals clear their lines, and say the latency pass is unsized until the repeated-run step reports. Either give a reason the 66 ms (about a quarter of the budget) should hold, or lower the confidence form.

prompt_lever's sentence contrasts different moves: +11.9 is Nano-XS going from zero-shot to few-shot, while +0.8 is Brisk-S going from few-shot to rubric + reasoning. To show that worked examples matter most for the smallest model, compare +11.9 with Brisk-S zero-shot to few-shot (+4.7, +4.2 to +5.2), or cite the interaction row (+7.2, +6.5 to +7.9). Both are already in the block.

nano_gap's caption says each row is the difference 'overall and in each place both hold it', but the block has no overall row. Add the overall row, Brisk-S few-shot less Nano-XS few-shot on balanced accuracy: +0.6, interval +0.2 to +1.0 (the flip of prompt_lever's -0.6, -1.0 to -0.2). Or drop 'overall' from the caption. Round the Simple × Science bound (-0.03699) to -0.04. The sentence 'what that buys is news' overstates the case: Simple × News leans the other way (-0.5) and Medium × News is +1.5. Say 'chiefly Complex × News'.

One gate goes by two names. Watch and the gate table call it 'Overall accuracy', while the headline, recommendation and method call it the balanced-accuracy gate. A reader could take 'overall accuracy' to mean traffic-weighted accuracy (92.2% for the pick), which would make the 0.7-point margin look like 2.2. Use 'balanced accuracy' everywhere the gate is named.

In 'What you could change', the latency row says that when the budget is loosened, slower options enter 'but each costs more, and the pick holds'. Above 496 ms, Brisk-S rubric (91.5%) and Atlas-M few-shot (92.1%) would pass every gate with higher balanced accuracy, so the pick would then rest on cost. The page says elsewhere that cost decides nothing and that its routing is unknown. Say the pick holds only if the lower cost is preferred to 0.8–1.4 more points of balanced accuracy.

findings.finding: In 'What you could change', the cell-floor row says that at a floor of 76.7% or below, Nano-XS few-shot 'becomes the pick'. The lede says the call would change if Nano-XS few-shot lifted Complex × News above the floor. Both leave out two conditions. Fix: in both places, say Nano-XS few-shot would take over only if it also holds the balanced-accuracy gate on a re-run, and only on cost as this run served it. The third next step already says this, so it only needs carrying up.

items.reason: Each block carries its claim's own figure, and every number I spot-checked matches the tool: monthly cost $1,200, gap +$1,143, 21×, 26.5%, 19,383, and interval half-widths of 1.4 and 1.2.
